intro_notes: NOTE: Scouts should obey all local fishing regulations and property laws.
NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in fishing activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Discuss the prevention of and treatment for the following health concerns that could occur while fishing: cuts and scratches, puncture wounds, insect bites, hypothermia, dehydration, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, and sunburn. (c) Explain how to remove a barbed hook that is lodged in someone's arm. (d) Name and explain five safety practices you should always follow while fishing.

pamphlet_excerpts: Orsomeone Group Shows: If you orsomeone in your group shows signs of a heat reaction, get to acool, shady place.
Person Lie Down: Have the person lie down with the feet, head, and shoulders slightly raised, and remove excess clothing.
Cool Victim Way: Cool the victim any way you can (cover the person with cool, wet towels, or sponge the person with cool water; fan the person; place the victim in a stream).
Not Rapid Recovery: If you do not see a rapid recovery, seek medical attention right away.
step_by_step_procedure: Sunburns First-degree Burns: Most sunburns are first-degree burns, but prolonged exposure to the suncan cause blistering, a second-degree burn.
Sunburn Easy Preventby: Sunburn is easy to preventby applying plenty of sunscreen and clothing with a sun protection factor (SPF) rating of at least 30.
Reapply Sweating Havebeen: Reapply if you are sweating and after you havebeen in water.
Broad-brimmed Hat: A broad-brimmed hat, long-sleeved shirt, and long pantsprovide even more protection.

Transparent Protectiveplates: Transparent protectiveplates growing from the skinthat can be replaced if lost.
step_by_step_procedure: Forward Fin Supported: The forward fin, supported by sharp spines, isused for balance.
Spines Alsoprotect Fish: The spines alsoprotect the fish from its predators.
Tackle Catalogs List: Tackle catalogs list rods and reels by weight and function, allowing the angler to make informed choices.
Afixed-line Pole Does: Afixed-line pole does not have a reel, and therefore is called a “pole” instead of a “rod.” Cane poles are usually made fromdried bamboo.

pamphlet_excerpts: Varieties Lines Different: Varieties of lines of different weights, diameters, and constructionare available, made for different types of fishing, fly-fishing, spin-fishing.
Monofilament Lines Come: Monofilament lines come labeledas nylon, which floats, and fluorocarbon, which sinks. allowingfor different delivery of lures and baits.
Lines Come Inclear: These lines come inclear, which is almost invisible to fish, and in colored lines fordifferent conditions.
Nylon Fluorocarbon: Nylon and fluorocarbon monofilamentlines are used when using a fixed-line pole, a closed-face spincasting reel, or an open-faced spinning reel.
step_by_step_procedure: Low-stretch Braidedlines: Low-stretch braidedlines are generally used in bait-casting and open-faced spinfishing.
Fly Lines Fly-fishing: Fly lines for fly-fishing are coated with a plastic finishto add weight.
They Come Level: They come level or tapered to facilitate casting.
Avoid Level Fly: Avoid the level fly line, as it is frustrating to cast.

pamphlet_excerpts: Knot combines Leaders Double: This knot combines two leaders, each with a double surgeon’s loop.
Theleaders Changed: Theleaders can be changed easily with this connection.
Start Layingthe Lines: Start by layingthe two lines to be joined with tagends in opposite directions, overlapping by six-plus inches.
Nowtake Overlapping Lines: Nowtake the overlapping lines andform a double overhand knot, passing the tag end and theentire shorter line through theloop twice.
step_by_step_procedure: Finish Moistening Knot: Finish by moistening the knot and pulling bothends tight.
Basic Knot Serves: This basic knot serves the same purpose as theimproved clinch knot.
Double Line Inch: Double the line to make a 3- to 4-inch loop, then pass the end of the loop through the hook eye.
Hold Thestanding Part: Hold thestanding part between thumb and forefinger and tie a loose overhand knot in the double line with the other hand.

pamphlet_excerpts: Plastic Wormsare Fished: Plastic wormsare fished slowly, on or near thebottom.
Withthe Texas Rig: Withthe Texas rig orweedless rig, thefish is allowed tomouth the baitbefore thehook is set.
Soft Pliable Lures: These soft, pliable lures in varying styles andshapes can be made to swim, wiggle, and dance underwater with an action the fish cannot resist.
They Plain Abare: They are used plain on abare hook, impaled on a jig, or effectively utilized with severalpopular rigs.
step_by_step_procedure: Bass Particularly Attracted: Bass are particularly attracted to these artificialworms, which the industry provides in different styles, shapes, and colors.
Scented Soft Baits: In addition, scented soft baits are available innumerous styles.

pamphlet_excerpts: Mind Not Fish: Keep in mind that not all fish should be filleted.
Removing Meat Somefish: Removing the meat of somefish from the bones and skin makes it easier to cook and to eat.
Lay Fish Its: Step 1, Lay the fish on its side and make a cut justbehind the gills down to the backbone, but not through it.
Start Cut Run: Step 2, Start at the cut made in step 1 and run the pointof the knife alongside the backbone, down to where itstarts to click along the tops of the ribs.
step_by_step_procedure: Cut Alongside Theribs: Cut alongside theribs, working back toward the tail until the entire side ofthe fish is free from the ribs and backbone, but leave itattached.
Lay Side Flat: Step 3, Lay the side flat and hook a forefinger under the skin near the tail.
Run Knife Meat: Run the knife into the meat next to the skin and hold the blade against the inside of the skin at anangle of about 45 degrees.
Holding Blade Steady: Holding the blade steady, gentlylift the forefinger holding the skin and pull.
